supporting_observations.claim: The alerted transfer is identifiable at 13:46:56 UTC: the proxy recorded 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes to ingest.cobaltvault.net:443, while network telemetry recorded 640,000,228 originating bytes on FILE-HD-01 source port 59207 to the explicit proxy.
Endpoint records attribute that same source-port-59207 connection to PID 5256, C:\Program Files\CobaltVault\Agent\cvagent.exe, running as HARBOR-DENTAL\svc-bkp.

PID 5256 was launched by services.exe at 13:46:45 UTC with command-line arguments '--job Nightly --target https://ingest.cobaltvault.net', using svc-bkp logon session 0x3ca0252. That session was recorded as a service logon.

The process path, service account, destination domain, and several-hundred-MB outbound volume match the approved CobaltVault backup activity described in the supplied inventory. Together with the exact connection-to-process correlation, this supports a benign disposition of the alerted transfer.

known_telemetry_limitations: The bulk connection is logged as a CONNECT tunnel; its application request, transferred files, and payload are not exposed in T020-00285 through T020-00288.
The inspected GET in T020-00282 belongs to the earlier source-port-62894 connection, not the bulk source-port-59207 connection. It does not establish the bulk transfer's HTTP method or content.
The process-creation records provide the executable path and command line but no executable hash or signature validation for cvagent.exe (T020-00278, T020-00279).
claims_not_established: The exact files transferred and successful completion of a backup job are not established by the connection counters or process termination records (T020-00285, T020-00286, T020-00292, T020-00293).
The unusual svc-bkp ticket request from 23.129.64.210 does not establish that the backup process or alerted transfer was attacker-controlled (T020-00264, T020-00278, T020-00288).
unrelated_findings: Open a separate account-security investigation: DC-HD-01 recorded a svc-bkp service-ticket request for FILE-HD-01 from 23.129.64.210 at 13:45:53 UTC, inconsistent with the supplied internal-only remote-administration context. This record alone does not establish compromise or control of the alerted transfer (T020-00264).
Review explicit svc-bkp credential use by PowerShell running as SYSTEM on WS-OHADDAD-01 at 13:35:19 UTC; authorization and purpose are not established by this record (T020-00147).

Open a separate remote-access policy ticket: lucy.park successfully logged on to FILE-HD-01 over RDP from WS-LPARK-01, contrary to the supplied practice allowing remote administration only from WS-OHADDAD-01. This occurred after the alerted transfer (T020-00342, T020-00349).

Review the FILE-HD-01 connection to config.zscaler.net with a Zscaler Client Connector user agent against the approved-software inventory; the record establishes the connection and claimed user agent, not installation or maliciousness (T020-00077).
